posts.cooked: I just wanted to point out that "he" is gender inclusive in English.  If the gender of someone is unknown or cannot be discerned (or, in this case, nonexistent), then "he" is an appropriate term to address "him" by.  Unless, of course, "he" objects to this term and ask that you use a different one.  If you persist at that point, you're kind of being a jerk.
